# SEO-225: Provide alt text for images that carry information

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `images` |
| Category | `ACCESSIBILITY` |

| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

An image conveying content a reader needs - a chart, a diagram, a photograph of the product, a screenshot, an image used as a link or a button - has alt text that conveys the same information in words.

## Rationale

Alt text is the only representation of the image available to a reader using a screen reader, to a browser that failed to load it, and to anything indexing the page as text, so an informative image without it simply has no content.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "has_images"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Write the text from what the image communicates in its context, not from the filename or a keyword list. Where the image is the content of a link, describe the destination rather than the picture. An automated agent may report a missing value but must not invent a description of an image it cannot see.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Collect every image element in the served response together with its alt attribute and role, and report informative images whose alt attribute is absent.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `ACCESSIBILITY_SCAN`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: `img-alt-attribute-present`

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `GOOGLE_IMAGES`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: none recorded.
